title: api: schema versioning - deprecations, beta headers, and backcompat shims for OpenAI compat
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: establish a controlled rollout for API request/response schema changes that affect streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output while preserving behavior for OpenAI-compat clients. This PR introduces a versioning header (Redwood-Schema-Version + optional X-Redwood-Beta header) to gate new fields and behaviour, a list of documented deprecations with migration guidance, and a lightweight compatibility shim layer in the OpenAI compatibility adapter to maintain behavioral parity during the migration window. Changes included: checklist: - [x] Add Redwood-Schema-Version header parsing and defaulting logic. - [x] Add X-Redwood-Beta header to opt into experimental schema v2 features. - [x] Introduce server-side backcompat shims in redwood-openai-compat to map v2 structured-output fields to v1 wire format for streaming clients. - [x] Stabilize streaming boundaries for function-calling and tool invocations to avoid truncated JSON objects across event chunks. - [x] End-to-end tests for streaming + function-calling with both v1 and v2 headers. - [x] Documentation updates and migration notes. Notes: The approach intentionally keeps the default behaviour unchanged (schema v1) unless clients opt-in via headers. The compatibility shims are limited in scope: they actively translate the v2 structured_output envelope to the legacy streaming delta format and synthesize legacy event types expected by the OpenAI-compatible SDKs. This is a short-term backcompat layer that will be removed after a 90-day deprecation window called out in docs. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan and telemetry gating.

release_notes: Introduce Redwood-Schema-Version header (defaults to 1). Clients can opt-in to v2 via X-Redwood-Beta: schema-v2.
Backward-compatibility shims added to openai-compat to preserve streaming and function-calling behavior for non-opted-in clients.
Structured output v2 envelope introduced under beta flag; migration guide included.
No changes to default behavior unless header is supplied.
backcompat_plan: Provide compatibility shims in openai-compat for 90 days after public announcement; emit telemetry on schema header usage; post-deprecation notices in Console and docs. Users must migrate to X-Redwood-Beta opt-in before shims are removed.
test_matrix_summary: Unit tests: pass; Integration tests: pass; E2E streaming tests: pass after two reruns for flaky decoder-test; Lint: pass; Canary: staged in perf-canary with no regressions
notes: We intentionally avoid touching client SDKs in this PR; SDK changes will follow in a separate PR that updates streaming parsers to support v2 structured envelopes. The openai-compat shims are documented as temporary.
